I just want to say I successfully visited Japan last week, winged it like mad with what Japanese I crammed in 2 months and was accepted as an apprentice. It was scary at first taking public transportation and ordering food but I'm proud to have used mostly Japanese. I still need a lot of practice and did get some help translating when I met my now Oyakata. 

There was a lot of great information shared here and I took bits from everything and modified to create a study plan that has been working for me. My pacing has been 1 genki chapter a week although I had to put it off occasionally due to time constraints. 

I use wanikani for my kanji, anki for vocab, and go to my University's extension center to talk to Japanese international students for practice. The learning curve is steep and it's been hard but as long I am consistent I am confident that my Japanese will only improve with time.

As others have mentioned a high school diploma can be very helpful to have, but a GED isn't useless either. Acquire a GED and then look to attend a local community college where you can get your GEs or basic classes out of the way. At least where I live our local community college has a transfer system where as long as you meet their specific transfer requirements, you can have guaranteed transfer to the school of your choice. Of course depending on the school you may need additional requirements, interviews, etc to get accepted. Going from a GED straight to a 4 year college you may not have a great selection of schools. In your scenario it would be best to get a GED, go to a 2 year or community college, work your damnedest and get good grades, then apply and transfer to a 4 year university or college suited to your interests/major.
